what_it_states: Scalar model only: a real-valued query f: D -> R with sensitivity Delta f over a neighbour relation N; (epsilon,delta)-DP with epsilon>0 and delta>0; additive noise. Section 2 (data-independent noise): an infinite-dimensional linear/DRO problem over all probability measures gamma on R minimizing the expected loss integral of c under the DP constraint for every (phi,A) in [-Delta f,Delta f] x F; Assumption 1 (two conditions on the loss c: R -> R_+), Assumption 2 (surjective query differences on [-Delta f,Delta f]); Observation 1; Lemma 1 (piecewise-constant restriction); Proposition 1 (finite upper-bound LP P(L,beta)); dual problem; Proposition 2 (weak duality); Lemma 2; Proposition 3 (finite lower-bound LP D(L,beta)); Theorem 1 (P-D gap below any xi for large support and fine grid, hence strong duality); Proposition 4 (exhibits loss functions satisfying one but not both conditions of Assumption 1 for which the bounding-scheme conclusion fails, i.e. the authors' minimality statement for Assumption 1). Section 3 (data-dependent noise): Markov kernels gamma(.|phi) over a bounded interval Phi of query outputs weighted by a density w; Assumption 3; Observation 2; Proposition 5 (upper-bound LP P'(L,beta)); dual; Proposition 6 (weak duality); Proposition 7 (lower-bound LP D'(L,beta)); Theorem 2 (convergence and strong duality). Section 4: non-uniform partitions with Corollary 1 (sandwich and convergence); cutting-plane Algorithm 1 with Observation 3 (finite termination); Algorithm 2 with Proposition 8 (maximum-privacy-shortfall constraint in O(N^3)); data-dependent separation in O(K^2 N) relegated to the authors' repository. Section 5.1: GUROBI-based numerics; Table 1 (Delta f=1, l1-loss) reports suboptimality of the best benchmarks, identified as the truncated Laplace mechanism and the Geng et al. 2020 lower bound; l2-loss results are stated to be qualitatively similar but relegated to the e-companion; Figures 3-5; a numerical observation that the optimal scalar noise distribution may be non-monotone; the introduction states the method may generalize to multi-dimensional queries as future work only.
what_it_does_not_state: No planar, R^2 or l1-diamond model; no pure epsilon-DP (delta=0) theorem; no closed-form all-law optimum; no all-law squared-Euclidean MSE value or selector in dimension two; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2 or its equality case; no rounded-core selector. Its all-law content is a convergent numerical LP bounding scheme for scalar (epsilon,delta>0) noise.
